title: Prove consecutive paired-star words need thin rank at least g q.
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Proof, for one schedule family. On the paired-star contract, if the two halves of every stage are adjacent and no thin map sits between those halves, the endpoint requires total thin rank at least `q g`. At `g=31`, `q=26` that bound is **806**. Five thin maps of rank 26 supply at most **130**, so this schedule has no endpoint. The projectors need not commute, and the off-diagonal block `B` may be nonzero.

This is a proof in the projector algebra plus a square-free monomial count. It is not a finite census of words or projectors, not a heuristic search, and not unrestricted nonexistence of the `g=31`, `q=26` profile. Nested intervals, crossed intervals, and a thin map placed between the two halves stay open. No witness is constructed.

No new kappa. The selected frontier stays `781451/250000000 = 0.003125804`. The older chronological floor `5q >= 4q+20` still passes at `q=26`. The commuting-projector theorem still requires 16 thin maps of unrestricted rank; this note does not replace it. The same algebra is uniform in `g` and `q`. This package certifies the `g=31`, `q=26` consequence only and states no `g=13`, `q=8` result.

## Task and overlap

Base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` (upstream `CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds` main, fetched 2026-11-10). Package: `research/g31-q26-consecutive-rank`. Head: `1750566c34c9fb117dc4afc4ce2bdacca7da036b`.

Catalogue card `joint-query-controller`, priority revision 8. Scope status: **changed**. The card asks about a changed query demand. The assigned question is the open `g=31`, `q=26` paired-star profile from Discussion #5593 and `research/coupled31-chronology` (PR #5747), restricted to consecutive halves.

Overlap snapshot at 2026-11-10, complete pagination: 895 open PRs and 6951 discussion records, plus local notes at the base commit. Nearest work:

- PR #5747 / `research/coupled31-chronology`: chronological floor and the commuting map-count. Leaves both large profiles unconstructed. This note uses that contract and adds the consecutive-halves rank bound.
- Open PR #6922 (`d58701c38d035e0b602e5050af379e2e77caf559`) and open PR #6940 (`9888af91b9f9e6dc55efd4172858a7d6093d484b`): `g=3`, `d=2` finite censuses. Both say those censuses do not lift to `g=31`, `q=26`. They are not inputs and were not re-run.
- `research/longer-coupled-port-caller` and `research/five-call-projector-rigidity` use different caller frames.

No open PR found that proves or constructs this consecutive `g=31`, `q=26` schedule. The `g=13`, `q=8` profile was not taken.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/g31-q26-consecutive-rank --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/g31-q26-consecutive-rank
```

Registered replay passed: `PASS_G31_Q26_CONSECUTIVE_RANK` with `lower_total_rank=806` and `profile_total_rank=130`. `scripts/check_research_commit.py --check-source-history` passed at `1750566c34c9fb117dc4afc4ce2bdacca7da036b`.

The checker proves the local stage factor in the quotient by `A^2=A` and `AB+BA=B`, both half orders, and requires the identity to fail if that second relation is dropped. It then checks the scalar full-call transport and the private gap monomials for every leaf and every between-stage gap at `g=31`, and the same identities at `g=1,2,3,4`. Those smaller counts are the same formal identity, not a projector census. It checks the gap-incidence count on every basis vector and `rank(I_52)=52` against an explicit rank-26 matrix.

Not run: a search over nested or internal placements, a census at `q=26`, native transport, Lean, Docker, and a selected-frontier replay. `make frontier6030-verify` was not run.

## Credit

The paired-star contract, the chronological rank floor, and the commuting map-count are from PR #5747 (Ali Romman), including PR #5673, PR #5631, and PR #5617. Cinna Davis supplied the controller/simplex lineage those packages retain. Open PRs #6922 and #6940 record the separate `g=3` finite censuses.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Linked from `research/g31-q26-consecutive-rank/TASK.json`:

- Can a thin map between the two halves of a stage meet the `g=31`, `q=26` endpoint with total thin rank 130? The scalar prefix stops while a stage is open. First step: the core-to-leaf coefficient of one internal gap in that stage's eigenbasis, with the off-diagonal blocks free.
- Can nested or crossing stage intervals with noncommuting projectors meet the same endpoint with five rank-26 maps? First step: the pure product of one crossed pair and one nested pair in the projector algebra, before any `q=26` search.

## Workflow feedback

`docs/research/current-priorities.md` on this main is still labelled priority revision 8 and quotes an older kappa. The selected record `781451/250000000` is the one used here. Fork `main` is not upstream main, so this draft is based on a pin of `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` rather than on fork `main`.
